How you can multiply your productivity by joining the 5AM club [Article]
Can someone regurgitate and refute/confirm this for me? It's too late and I'm lazy.

A complete crock from a clickbait blog. Here's an archive anyway.

  • "Look at these three famous people who sleep odd hours! It's proof!"

  • Points one and two argue that distractions early in the morning will 1) drain your willpower, of which there is a finite amount per day and 2) reduce your focus. It's true that being distracted . This has nothing to do with waking up early or late, though. Rather than wake up before everyone else, you can just ignore them until you're done.

  • Point three says waking up in the morning is the best time to start a ritual, and rituals make you more consistent with habits you'd otherwise skip or procrastinate on. However, waking up early has absolutely nothing to do with this. You can wake up any time and start a morning routine. It's just how you manage the rest of the day around that.

  • Point four says you need to spend time alone to think and plan, free of distraction. Again, somehow they decide that waking up early is the only way to accomplish this.

  • Point five just says "there is something about getting up early before most of your competition that makes you feel like you are on top of your game" and provides no scientific explanation. Anecdotal evidence at best.

The article finishes by saying it was written "for you to understand the importance of knocking off your most valuable tasks and creating good habits first," which completely contradicts the thrust of the headline. Rather, one can summarize the facts more correctly by saying that you should hit your priorities as early as possible and do them every day, while also getting a chance to think before the details of the day ahead of you tie up your thoughts. I can say that it works for me.

I would like to counter that getting enough sleep is one of the most important things one can do. It is involved in everything from improving retention of knowledge to building muscle. Getting 8 or more hours is the #1 priority. (Short afternoon naps are also not a bad idea.) If you deprive yourself of sleep to wake up early, you're fucking yourself over for nothing.

I saw that too and thought that there's the unwritten assumption that you're a 9-5 worker. IE, to work on your personal goals you need to get up early and do it before work brings you down. He makes this assumption more explicit in his other article on finite willpower.
